title: The degree of a pulled-back locally free module along a nonconstant morphism of proper curves is multiplied by the degree of the morphism
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves deg(f^*E) = deg(X/Y) deg(E) for a nonconstant morphism of proper curves and a locally free E on the target. The proof recalls that the degree of X over Y is the rank of f_*O_X as a coherent sheaf on Y, namely the dimension of its stalk at the generic point, and then telescopes the Euler characteristic: chi(X, f^*E) = chi(Y, f_*f^*E) = chi(Y, E tensor f_*O_X) = deg(X/Y) deg(E) + n chi(Y, f_*O_X) = deg(X/Y) deg(E) + n chi(X, O_X) (proof lines 9906-9922). Each equality is then justified by finiteness of f, the projection formula, and the rank formula for the degree (proof lines 9923-9927). H2: the telescoping computation and the identification of the degree with the generic rank of f_*O_X are the substance.
